Baseline.d: A measurement of how things are before you change anything, such as how long test design takes today. Without a baseline you can't show that AI made a difference.

ROI.d: Return on investment: how much value you get back compared with what you spend. ROI = (benefit − cost) ÷ cost, usually shown as a percentage.

Escaped defect.d: A bug that got past testing and was found later, usually by customers or in production.

Flaky test.d: An automated test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any change to the code, usually because of timing, test data or environment problems.

Cycle time.d: How long a piece of work takes from start to finish, for example from a story being ready for testing to it being signed off.

MTTR.d: Mean time to repair (or resolve): the average time from noticing a failure to fixing it. In QA it often means how long a failing test or build takes to diagnose and fix.

Goodhart's law.d: The observation that when a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure, because people start optimising the number instead of the real goal.

Vanity metric.d: A number that looks impressive but doesn't show real value, such as 'number of AI prompts sent' or 'test cases generated'.

Leading indicator.d: An early measurement that suggests where results are heading, such as requirement questions raised before development. A lagging indicator, such as escaped defects, shows results only after the fact.

Pilot.d: A small, time-boxed trial of a new way of working with a few people and clear success criteria, run before rolling it out widely.

AI champion.d: A team member who learns a new tool early, helps colleagues, collects good practices and feeds problems back to the people running the rollout.

Maturity model.d: A set of levels describing how far an organisation has progressed with a practice, with checklists for what each level looks like.
